text: James, course one zero five, speed sixteen knots, on autopilot. No traffic close. That's all.
Thanks, Mateo. I have the watch.
Enjoy the bridge, cadet! Lunch for me now.
Right, Diego. Your first time on the bridge at sea. Let me show you the equipment.
Great. Is this the radar?
No, that's the ECDIS, the electronic chart. It shows our position. This one is the radar. It shows other ships.
In fog too?
In fog, at night, always. Remember Galveston?
I do! And what does this do?
That's the echo sounder. It measures the depth under the ship. Here, forty metres.
And the steering wheel?
We call it the helm. Now the autopilot steers, but we can change to hand steering any time.
This is the gyro compass. It gives the heading. And this lever is the engine telegraph.
And the binoculars?
For the lookout. But remember: the most important equipment on the bridge is your eyes.
My eyes. Got it.
Where's the ECDIS?
Show me the gyro compass.
Show me the helm.
Where are the binoculars?
Show me the echo sounder.
Where's the engine telegraph?
Diego, what does the radar do?
And the echo sounder? What does it do?
Hey cadet, what's this screen?
What does the gyro compass do?
The echo sounder shows twenty-five metres.
The autopilot steers. I watch.
